# **Introduction to Project** {#introduction-to-project}

In many small to mid-sized organizations, the recruitment process is often managed manually or through isolated tools such as spreadsheets, emails, and standalone job portals. This fragmented approach leads to delays, miscommunication, and lack of visibility across different stages of hiring. As a result, organizations face difficulties in attracting, tracking, and selecting the right candidates efficiently.

Our project aims to solve this problem by developing an integrated, web based **Recruitment Management System** named **HireFlow**. HireFlow will serve as a centralized platform to streamline the entire hiring lifecycle from job posting and applicant tracking to interview scheduling and final selection. By digitizing and automating key recruitment tasks, the system will enhance collaboration between HR personnel, recruitment managers, and applicants, reduce administrative overhead, and ensure a faster, more transparent hiring process.

# **Project Goal** {#project-goal}

The goal of **HireFlow** is to design and develop a centralized, user-friendly Recruitment Management System that streamlines and automates the end-to-end hiring process within an organization. The system aims to eliminate the inefficiencies of manual recruitment workflows by providing tools for job posting, applicant tracking, interview scheduling, and decision making all within a unified platform.

**HireFlow** will empower HR teams, recruitment managers, and system administrators to collaborate effectively, reduce time-to-hire, and improve the quality of candidate evaluation. By ensuring transparency, real-time tracking, and organized communication, HireFlow will support data-driven hiring decisions and contribute to building a more efficient and scalable recruitment process.

# **Scope of the project** {#scope-of-the-project}

## 3.1   Main Users {#3.1-main-users}

**System Admin:**  
The System Administrator is responsible for the overall technical maintenance and configuration of the HireFlow system. Their duties include managing user accounts and roles, resetting passwords, configuring system settings, and monitoring system logs for security and performance. The System Admin does not participate in recruitment workflows or applicant evaluations and does not handle job postings or candidate data.

**HR Admin:**  
The HR Admin manages the core operational aspects of the recruitment process. This includes creating and publishing job postings, managing applicant data, scheduling interviews, updating application statuses, and coordinating communication with applicants. The HR Admin works closely with Recruitment Managers to facilitate a smooth and efficient hiring pipeline but does not have access to system level settings or technical configurations.

**Recruitment Manager:**  
The Recruitment Manager is responsible for evaluating and managing candidates throughout the selection process. This includes reviewing applications, shortlisting candidates, conducting or attending interviews, and submitting interview feedback. Recruitment Managers collaborate with HR Admins to make final hiring decisions but do not have permissions to post new jobs or modify system settings.

**Applicant:**  
The Applicant is an external user who interacts only with the candidate-facing features of HireFlow. Applicants can browse job postings, create and update personal profiles, upload resumes and supporting documents, apply for jobs, and track the status of their applications. Applicants have no access to internal administrative functions, interview data, or other users’ information.

## 3.2   In-Scope(Main Functionalities) {#3.2-in-scope(main-functionalities)}

The following recruitment operations and related functionalities will be included in the scope of the HireFlow system by the end of the project:

#### **User and Role Management**

System shall allow the System Admin to create, update, and delete user accounts.  
System shall support role based access control for System Admin, HR Admin, Recruitment Manager, and Applicant.  
The system shall allow assigning and managing permissions for each user type.

#### **Job Posting Management**

HR Admin shall be able to create, edit, publish, and delete job postings.  
Job postings shall include details such as title, description, department, location, and deadline.  
The system shall support status control for jobs (e.g., Open, Closed, Draft).  
Applicants shall be able to browse and search available job postings.

#### **Application Management**

Applicants shall be able to apply for jobs through a web form and upload resumes and supporting documents.  
The system shall store applicant data including personal information, resume, and application history.  
HR Admin and Recruitment Manager shall be able to view, filter, and sort applicant records.  
System shall allow HR to update the status of each application (e.g., Shortlisted, Rejected, Offered).

#### **Interview Scheduling**

HR Admin shall be able to schedule interviews with shortlisted candidates.  
The system shall allow assigning interviewers and scheduling time slots.  
Applicants shall be notified of scheduled interviews via email or in-system alerts.

#### **Interview Feedback and Evaluation**

Recruitment Managers shall be able to submit interview feedback and rate candidates.  
Feedback forms may include criteria-based rating and optional comments.  
HR Admin shall review and consolidate interview results for final hiring decisions.

#### **Application Status Tracking and Notifications**

The system shall track each application's progress through stages (Applied, Shortlisted, Interview, Offered, etc.).  
Applicants shall be able to log in and view real-time updates on their application status.  
The system shall send notifications to applicants on key actions (e.g., shortlisted, rejected, interview scheduled).

#### **Reports and Analytics**

The system shall provide summary reports such as the number of applicants per job, hiring rate, and stage-wise drop-offs.  
HR Admin and Recruitment Manager shall be able to generate basic recruitment performance metrics.

## 3.3   Out-of-Scope {#3.3-out-of-scope}

The following functionalities will **not** be covered in the current version of HireFlow:

**Payroll Integration**: Generating salary slips, managing payroll cycles, and linking with finance modules.

**Employee Onboarding**: Post-hire activities such as contract generation, employee induction, and orientation.

**Training and Development**: Tracking candidate skill development, training modules, or learning management.

**Job Portal Integration**: Automatic job posting to third-party platforms like LinkedIn or Indeed.

**AI-based Resume Screening**: Automated parsing or shortlisting using machine learning or natural language processing.

**Video Interviews**: Integration with video conferencing tools or in system video interview functionality.

## 3.4   Flow of Events in the Current Context {#3.4-flow-of-events-in-the-current-context}

In many small to mid sized organizations, the recruitment process is still managed using spreadsheets, emails, and disconnected job portals. Job openings are often shared manually or posted on separate websites without a centralized tracking system. Applications are received via email, making it difficult to organize candidate information, maintain version control, or ensure consistency across evaluations.

Shortlisting and interview coordination are typically handled through back-and-forth emails or verbal communication, leading to scheduling conflicts and miscommunication among HR staff and recruitment managers. Applicant status updates are rarely automated, leaving candidates unaware of their progress. As a result, the recruitment process becomes time-consuming, error-prone, and lacks transparency.

These fragmented workflows not only delay hiring decisions but also create a poor experience for both applicants and hiring teams. There is a clear need for an integrated system that streamlines job posting, applicant tracking, interview management, and communication all in one place.

## 3.5   Flow of Events with HireFlow {#3.5-flow-of-events-with-hireflow}

With HireFlow:

**HR Admins** create and manage job postings through a centralized dashboard, specifying job details, requirements, and deadlines.

**Applicants** can register, browse available job listings, and apply directly through the system by filling out application forms and uploading resumes or supporting documents.

**HR Admins** and **Recruitment Managers** can view and filter applications, shortlist candidates, and schedule interviews all from within the platform.

**Recruitment Managers** provide structured feedback after interviews using built-in evaluation forms, enabling informed and collaborative hiring decisions.

**Applicants** are automatically notified about their application status at every stage (e.g., shortlisted, rejected, interview scheduled), ensuring transparency and reducing communication delays.

The **System Admin** manages user accounts, access levels, and system preferences to maintain a secure and well-organized environment.

All users benefit from real-time updates, clear process visibility, and reduced manual overhead leading to a faster, more efficient, and consistent recruitment experience.

# **Objectives of the project** {#objectives-of-the-project}

1. **To automate the recruitment process**  
   Replace fragmented, manual hiring workflows with a centralized system that allows HR Admins to manage job postings, track applicants, and oversee the entire recruitment lifecycle from a single interface.

2. **To enable structured job posting and application intake**  
   Allow HR Admins to create and publish job vacancies directly through the system. Enable Applicants to view listings and submit their applications online, along with resumes and supporting documents.

3. **To streamline candidate evaluation and interview coordination**  
   Provide tools for Recruitment Managers to review applications, shortlist candidates, schedule interviews, and submit structured interview feedback, ensuring a consistent and organized selection process.

4. **To provide real-time application tracking and status updates**  
   Allow Applicants to track the progress of their application throughout each stage of the hiring pipeline, with automatic status updates and notifications that keep them informed.

5. **To enforce role-based access control across the recruitment system**  
   Ensure that each user System Admin, HR Admin, Recruitment Manager, or Applicant has access only to the functionalities relevant to their role, thereby improving data privacy, usability, and operational clarity..

6. **To enhance communication between hiring teams and applicants**  
   Enable in-system notifications to keep users informed about key events, such as interview schedules, status changes, or feedback submissions reducing reliance on emails and verbal communication.

7. **To increase transparency and decision-making efficiency**  
   Track every stage of the hiring process with audit trails and reports, helping HR and management monitor performance metrics and identify bottlenecks in recruitment workflows.

8. **To ensure secure storage and access of applicant data**  
   Protect sensitive personal information submitted by applicants using proper access controls and data handling practices, in compliance with security and privacy guidelines.

# **Project Feasibility** {#project-feasibility}

## 5.1   Technical Feasibility {#5.1-technical-feasibility}

In this section, we evaluate whether the proposed **Recruitment Management System – HireFlow** can be successfully developed using currently available technologies, tools, and resources. We also assess whether the selected technologies are sufficient to implement the required features of the system.

**Front-End Development**:

HTML and CSS are used to design responsive, user-friendly interfaces for both internal users (HR Admins, Recruitment Managers, System Admins) and external users (Applicants). These technologies ensure cross-browser compatibility and allow customization for different user experiences such as dashboards, job listings, and application forms. 

**Back-End Development**:

PHP: PHP acts as the server-side scripting language, handling the core recruitment logic such as job creation, application submission, user authentication, interview scheduling, and status tracking. PHP will interact with the MySQL database to retrieve and update applicant and job-related data.

MySQL: MySQL is used as the Relational Database Management System (RDBMS) for managing all persistent data in HireFlow. This includes job postings, applicant records, user credentials, interview schedules, feedback, and application statuses.

**MVC Architecture**:  
The application is built using the **Model-View-Controller (MVC)** architectural pattern, which separates data handling, business logic, and presentation layers:

* **Model:** Manages database interactions and application data (e.g., applicant records, job listings).  
* **View:** Delivers the UI to users using HTML/CSS, allowing different interfaces for each user role.  
* **Controller:** Handles HTTP requests and links the model and view, e.g., processing job applications or routing interview feedback.

### 5.1.1.  IDEs {#5.1.1.-ides}

* **Visual Studio Code (VS Code) :**A powerful and extensible code editor ideal for full-stack web development. It supports syntax highlighting and debugging for HTML, CSS, PHP, and SQL, with extensions for Git and live server integration.  
    
* **MySQL Workbench :** A visual tool for database design, schema management, and SQL query execution, aiding in the design and management of the recruitment-related database schema.

### 5.1.2.  Tools & Utilities {#5.1.2.-tools-&-utilities}

* **Web Browsers :**Google Chrome, Mozilla Firefox – Used for testing and debugging user interfaces for different users such as HR Admins, Applicants, and Recruitment Managers.

* **XAMPP Server :** A local development environment that includes Apache (web server), MySQL (database), and PHP. It enables testing the full-stack application on a local machine before deployment.

* **phpMyAdmin :** A browser-based tool to manage the MySQL database. It provides an easy interface for testing queries and viewing applicant/job data directly.  
    
* **Git/GitHub :** Used for source control and collaboration among team members. It helps track changes, manage branches, and streamline teamwork in a group development environment.

* **Figma/Draw.io :**  Used for creating visual artifacts like wireframes, ER diagrams, use case diagrams, and workflow charts that illustrate the system design and logic of HireFlow.

### 5.1.3.  Hardware {#5.1.3.-hardware}

* Developer Machines   
  Each team member requires a computer with at least a modern web browser, code editor (VS Code), and enough processing power to run XAMPP, MySQL, and browser-based testing tools simultaneously. A stable internet connection is also required for version control and resource access.

## 5.2   Operational Feasibility {#5.2-operational-feasibility}

This section evaluates whether the proposed **HireFlow** system effectively addresses existing recruitment-related issues and integrates well within the organization’s operational environment.

* **Automation of Recruitment Tasks:**  
  HireFlow digitizes core recruitment functions such as job posting, applicant tracking, interview scheduling, and feedback collection, replacing manual and disjointed processes.

* **Improved Efficiency and Accuracy:**  
  The system reduces paperwork, administrative workload, and human errors, resulting in a faster and more reliable hiring process.  
    
* **User-Friendly Interface:**  
  Designed with simplicity in mind, HireFlow requires only basic computer skills to operate and offers an intuitive interface for both internal users and external applicants.  
    
* **Minimal Training and Easy Adoption:**  
  With guided workflows and role-based dashboards, the system fits smoothly into existing operations and requires minimal training for effective use.

## 5.3   Legal & Ethical Feasibility {#5.3-legal-&-ethical-feasibility}

This section ensures that **HireFlow** complies with applicable laws, ethical standards, and best practices when handling user data, system access, and digital resources.

1. **Data Security & Privacy :** THireFlow must protect sensitive applicant and user data such as names, emails, phone numbers, resumes, and interview feedback. Only authorized users (e.g., HR Admins, Recruitment Managers) should have access to specific data based on their role. Measures like password protection, secure session handling, and encrypted data storage must be used to prevent unauthorized access or data breaches.

2. ** Role-Based Access Control  :** Each user in the system such as System Admin, HR Admin, Recruitment Manager, or Applicant can only access the functionalities relevant to their role

3. **No Illegal Software :** All tools and platforms used in the development of HireFlow (such as VS Code, XAMPP, MySQL, phpMyAdmin, and Git) are open-source or legally licensed. No cracked, pirated, or unauthorized software is used. This ensures the project is compliant with software licensing regulations.

4. **Compliance with Data Protection Laws :** If deployed for real-world use, HireFlow must comply with applicable data protection laws.  
* Informing applicants and users how their data is collected and used  
* Requesting consent before storing personal information  
* Providing users the option to view, update, or delete their personal data upon request


5. **Ethical Usage of the System :** HireFlow must be used fairly and ethically, respecting the rights and dignity of all users, especially job applicants.  
* Personal data must not be misused for bias, discrimination, or unjust decisions (e.g., rejecting a candidate based on irrelevant personal info).  
* The system must not be used to monitor users secretly or access applicant information without purpose or permission.  
* Fair hiring practices must be promoted through transparent workflows and access policies.

	

## 5.4   Social Feasibility {#5.4-social-feasibility}

This section evaluates how well the **HireFlow** system aligns with workplace culture, user expectations, and social impact within the organization.

1. **User Acceptance :** HireFlow is designed to simplify recruitment tasks for all users involved. HR personnel can manage applicants and job postings efficiently, while recruitment managers can access candidate data and provide feedback from a centralized dashboard. Applicants benefit from a smoother, more accessible application experience without the need for in-person follow-ups.  
     
2. **Improved Transparency :** The system ensures that every action, such as shortlisting, rejection, or scheduling is logged and traceable. Applicants can view their real-time application status, eliminating the need to rely on verbal communication or email queries. This promotes fairness and accountability throughout the hiring process.

3. **No Job Loss Risk :** HireFlow does not replace HR staff or recruitment managers; instead, it assists them by automating routine administrative tasks. Core decisions like candidate selection and communication still require human involvement. The system is a supportive tool, not a replacement for human roles in recruitment.

4. **Promotes Paperless Work :** All application-related data including resumes, interview feedback, and status updates are managed digitally within the system. This eliminates the need for physical documents, folders, or manual filing. HireFlow supports environmentally friendly practices while fostering a modern, paperless work culture.

## 5.5   Economic Feasibility {#5.5-economic-feasibility}

This section checks if the **HireFlow** project is affordable to build, run, and maintain.

1. **Low Development Cost :**The system is being developed by university students as part of an academic project, which eliminates the need to hire professional software developers. As a result, development involves no financial expense beyond the team’s time and effort.  
     
2. **Free Tools :** HireFlow is built using free and open-source tools such as Visual Studio Code, XAMPP, PHP, and MySQL. There are no paid licenses required, keeping software costs at zero  
   .  
3. **No Additional Hardware(Currently in out scope) :** Each team member is using their personal PC or laptop for development and testing. The system runs locally using XAMPP, so no servers, printers, or dedicated hardware are required at this stage.  
     
4. **Maintenance Cost :** Since HireFlow is a small, local web application, ongoing maintenance is minimal. Simple updates such as adding new job fields or fixing minor bugs can be made by any developer without significant cost or effort.  
     
5. **Long-Term Benefit :** HireFlow reduces the administrative workload and eliminates the need for manual recruitment tracking. Over time, this leads to savings in human effort, paperwork, and time, providing a high return on investment for organizations that adopt it.  
 


## 5.6   Schedule Feasibility {#5.6-schedule-feasibility}

This checks whether the **HireFlow** project can be completed within the given university timeline.

1. **Small and Manageable Scope** : The system includes only essential modules such as job posting, application tracking, interview scheduling, and user management. Each team member is assigned four CRUD-based operations, making the workload balanced and manageable.  
     
2. **Clear Task Division** : All four group members have clearly defined roles with equal responsibilities. Development tasks are distributed evenly, allowing the team to work in parallel and avoid bottlenecks.  
     
3. **No Complex Features** : HireFlow focuses only on core functionalities, no external integrations like payment gateways, SMS APIs, or advanced analytics. This ensures that development stays focused on basic CRUD operations and straightforward user interfaces.  
     
4. **Risk of Delay** : Delays may occur only if a group member fails to complete their assigned CRUD tasks on time. However, since the workload is realistic and limited in scope, the risk of project delay remains low. 

# **Deliverables of the project** {#deliverables-of-the-project}

**Working Recruitment Management System (HireFlow) Web Application**

A fully functional, web-based **Recruitment Management System** developed using core web technologies (HTML, CSS, JavaScript, PHP, and MySQL). The system will support:

* Job posting and vacancy management  
* Applicant registration and application submission  
* Interview scheduling and feedback collection

    
* Application status tracking and notifications  
  The application will include secure login-based access control and distinct user interfaces for System Admins, HR Admins, Recruitment Managers, and External Applicants.

** **  
**Technical Documentation**

A complete and well-structured technical report that includes:

* System architecture and key design decisions  
* Use case models and modular breakdown  
* Database schema and ER diagrams specific to recruitment workflows  
* Implementation structure (file organization, logic flow)  
* Development tools, platforms, and frameworks used

This documentation will assist future developers, evaluators, or maintainers in understanding or extending **HireFlow**.

   
**User Guide**

A user-friendly manual designed for non-technical users, explaining how each system user can perform their tasks. It will detail:

* How to log in and navigate their dashboard  
* Role-specific functions (e.g., posting jobs, applying, reviewing applications, scheduling interviews)  
* Understanding and responding to system-generated notifications


The guide will feature step-by-step instructions, annotated screenshots, and helpful tips for all roles: System Admin, HR Admin, Recruitment Manager, and Applicant.

# **Project Constraints and Assumptions** {#project-constraints-and-assumptions}

## 7.1  Constraints {#7.1-constraints}

**Job Applications Are Allowed Only for Active Job Postings**  
Applicants can only apply to jobs currently marked as “Open” by the HR Admin. Closed, expired, or unpublished job posts will not be displayed or accessible..

**One Application Per Job Vacancy per Applicant**  
An applicant is allowed to apply only once for a specific job post. Multiple submissions for the same vacancy by the same applicant are restricted.

**Resume Upload Is Mandatory for All Applications**  
Every job application must include a resume or CV file. Applications without an uploaded resume will be rejected by the system automatically.

**Only HR Admin Can Create or Edit Job Posts**  
 Job postings can only be created, edited, or removed by the HR Admin. Recruitment Managers and Applicants do not have permission to alter job listings.

**Applicants Cannot Edit Submitted Applications**  
Once an application is submitted, it cannot be edited or updated by the applicant. Any corrections or updates require a new application if the vacancy is still open.

**Only Recruitment Managers Can Provide Interview Feedback**  
 Interview evaluation forms and candidate feedback entries are restricted to Recruitment Managers. HR Admins can view but not modify evaluation results.

**Interviews Must Be Scheduled for Shortlisted Candidates Only**  
The system only allows interview scheduling for candidates who have been shortlisted. Candidates not in the shortlist cannot be assigned interview slots.

**No Anonymous Applications Allowed**  
 All applicants must create an account with valid contact information before applying. Anonymous or guest applications are not supported.

## 7.2  Assumptions {#7.2-assumptions}

**All Job Post Details Entered by HR Are Accurate and Up to Date**  
It is assumed that job postings created by the HR Admin are valid, properly described, and updated regularly to reflect current recruitment needs.

**Applicants Will Submit Genuine and Updated Resumes**  
The system assumes that all resumes uploaded by applicants are truthful and represent their actual qualifications. No automated verification is done.

**Interview Feedback Entered by Managers Is Fair and Honest**  
Recruitment Managers are expected to evaluate candidates ethically and enter honest feedback. The system does not verify or review evaluation fairness.

**All System Users Have Basic Digital Literacy**  
 It is assumed that HR Admins, Recruitment Managers, and Applicants can navigate the system and use features like uploading files, submitting forms, and checking notifications.

**All Recruitment Is Conducted in a Single Time Zone**  
 Interview scheduling and application deadlines are based on a single organizational time zone. Time zone conversions for remote hiring are not handled.

**Applicant Contact Information Is Accurate**  
It is assumed that email addresses and phone numbers provided by applicants are correct and active. The system does not verify contact details beyond format validation.

## 8.2   Quality attributes

### 8.2.1  Security {#8.2.1-security}

Role-based access control will ensure that only authorized users (HR Admin, Recruitment Manager, Applicant, System Admin) can access relevant system features and data.

A secure login system using username and password will be implemented to protect applicant and recruitment data.

Sensitive applicant information (e.g., resumes, contact details) will be stored securely with restricted access and proper session handling.

### 8.2.2  Availability {#8.2.2-availability}

Proper error handling will be used to ensure that critical modules (e.g., job posting, application submission) remain available even if non-critical components (e.g., notifications) experience failures.

Graceful degradation and fallback messages will be shown to maintain usability during partial system errors.

### 8.2.3  Modifiability {#8.2.3-modifiability}

The system will follow modular architecture, allowing future extensions like onboarding, referral tracking, or analytics modules.

Frontend, backend, and database components will be clearly separated to support easy updates or changes without impacting the whole system.

Code will be well-documented to support long-term maintainability.

### 8.2.4  Performance {#8.2.4-performance}

HireFlow will be optimized to ensure key pages (e.g., job listings, application forms, dashboard) load within 2 seconds under normal usage conditions.

SQL queries will be optimized to reduce database latency, especially during application filtering or status updates.

### 8.2.5  Testability {#8.2.5-testability}

Each module (job posting, application submission, shortlisting, interview scheduling) will be tested independently.

Unit testing will be conducted for backend functions such as user authentication, application submission, and status updates.

Manual testing will be performed for different user roles to ensure end-to-end functionality and workflow correctness.

### 8.2.6  Usability {#8.2.6-usability}

The user interface will be clean, consistent, and easy to navigate for users with basic computer skills, including applicants with no prior system experience.

Clear field labels, progress indicators, and validation messages will help users complete actions confidently.

Different dashboards will be customized for each role, ensuring simplicity and relevance in the user experience.

# 

# **Technologies to be used** {#technologies-to-be-used}

## 9.1   Front-end development of the web application {#9.1-front-end-development-of-the-web-application}

The View layer in the MVC architecture will be developed using:

* **HTML5:** For structuring UI components such as job listings, application forms, dashboards, and content layouts.  
* **CSS3:** To style the interface with responsive design principles, ensuring usability across devices and screen sizes.  
* **Vanilla JavaScript:** For client-side interactivity, dynamic updates of job statuses, form validation, and real-time notifications.

The View will remain separate from business logic and will be rendered dynamically by PHP controllers as required.

## 9.2   Back-end development of the web application {#9.2-back-end-development-of-the-web-application}

The Controller and Model layers will be implemented using:

**PHP (Plain, without frameworks):**

* Controllers will handle user requests such as job postings, application submissions, interview scheduling, and route them to appropriate models.

* Models will contain business logic and interact with the database to manage data related to users, job vacancies, applications, and interviews.

**MySQL:**

* Used for persistent storage of job posts, applicant profiles, interview feedback, user accounts, and system logs.  
* Model classes will encapsulate SQL queries and data manipulation.

**XAMPP:**

* Provides Apache web server, MySQL database, and PHP runtime environment for local development, testing, and deployment simulation.

The MVC folder structure will be maintained (e.g., /models/, /views/, /controllers/), and routing will be manually handled through custom PHP logic.

## 9.3   CASE tools for the system development process {#9.3-case-tools-for-the-system-development-process}

The following tools will assist in designing and modeling system components during the software development lifecycle:

* **Draw.io:**  
   For creating UML diagrams such as Use Case Diagrams, Activity Diagrams, and Component Diagrams specific to recruitment workflows.

* **Visual Studio Code (VS Code):**  
   Primary IDE for writing HTML, CSS, JavaScript, and PHP, and managing the MVC project structure.

* **Git:**  
   For version control, enabling collaborative development and change tracking.

* **ClickUp:**  
   For task management, project planning, and team collaboration throughout the development process.

# **Project timeline** {#project-timeline}

The development of HireFlow will follow an **Iterative Waterfall** model. In this method, every phase contains a feedback path to its previous phase. So, with any feedback or insights received we can go back and make changes to be more aligned with the requirements and the goals of the project. The project will be completed over a period of **10 months (June 2025 – March 2026\)**
